title: WKT Coordinate Counter: Pairs in a Geometry
description: Count the coordinate pairs inside a WKT geometry with the WKT Coordinate Counter — vertices per ring and part, tallied locally. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a POLYGON whose outer ring lists 5 pairs and whose hole lists 4 holds 9 coordinate pairs — with the closing pair of each ring counted, because in WKT it is written, so it counts.
quick_answer: The WKT Coordinate Counter counts the coordinate pairs inside a Well-Known Text geometry — every vertex of every ring, line and member — and breaks the total down by part. Paste the WKT and read how many positions the geometry actually carries.

body.t: Vertex count predicts rendering cost, payload size and simplification benefit better than file size does. Compare before and after a simplify pass — the
works the same trade on GeoJSON.
A POLYGON ring whose first and last pairs match is closed; counting pairs per ring helps spot the ring that forgot to come home.
A 'simple boundary' column holding 400,000-pair monsters explains the slow queries — the counter proves which rows are the monsters.
WKT in, GeoJSON out: pair counts should survive conversion (modulo ring-closure conventions). Count both sides with their own counters and reconcile.

A square POLYGON ring written with 5 pairs (the fifth repeating the first to close) counts 5, not 4 — the counter counts what is written. Some formats store 4 and imply closure; conversions differ by exactly the ring count, and this is where that off-by-one lives.
A MULTILINESTRING of three lines with 12, 40 and 7 pairs totals 59 — reported per part as well as summed, because the 40-pair part is where the weight (and the simplification win) sits.

popular_table.note: Z and M ordinates ride inside the pairs; a pair is a position regardless of how many numbers dress it.

faq: POINT with Z — still one pair?
Yes — one position with three ordinates. The counter counts positions, not numbers.
POINT EMPTY and friends count as zero, reported as the valid empties they are.
GEOMETRYCOLLECTION members recurse — a collection of collections counts to the bottom.
Why would two files of one boundary differ by exactly the ring count?
Closure convention: one writer repeats the first pair per ring, another doesn't. The difference equals the number of rings — a fingerprint, not an error.
Their control points are countable tuples; true arc vertices are implied geometry beyond tuple counting — the count reports the written control points, labelled as such.
The parse is linear in the text; million-pair geometries count in seconds in the browser.
Can it count only unique positions?
Duplicates (including closing pairs) count as written. Uniqueness is an analysis choice, not a counting default.
